req.title: Redirect once when n==1
req.statement: The system shall respond with a single 302 to /get when /redirect/1 is called.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /redirect/1 must issue exactly one 302 redirect to /get, and the final response (after following the redirect) must be HTTP 200 with the expected JSON payload. We need: (1) a positive test confirming the 302 → /get chain works correctly with exact status codes and Location header; (2) a negative test confirming that /redirect/0 is rejected (assert=n>0 triggers 500); (3) a boundary test at n=1 (the exact threshold where the code switches from the recursive path to the direct redirect to view_get). Additional tests cover the redirect-not-followed path (raw 302 with exact Location), and the n=2 boundary to confirm the different code path is taken. This covers EP, BVA, NEG, STC, and DT heuristics and is designed to kill mutations on the n==1 comparison, the redirect target, and the status code constants.

tests.name: test_redirect_1_returns_302_with_location_to_get
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client with follow_redirects=False
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_1_returns_302_with_location_to_get():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert location.endswith('/get'), f'Expected Location ending with /get, got: {location}'

test_redirect_1_returns_302_with_location_to_get()

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_1_boundary_exact_location_header():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.status_code != 301
    assert r.status_code != 200
    location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert location == '/get', f'Expected exactly /get, got: {location}'

tests.name: test_redirect_2_does_not_go_directly_to_get
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
n=2 is n==1+1, should NOT redirect directly to /get but to /redirect/1
actions: Create Flask test client with follow_redirects=False
expected: Location header does NOT equal '/get' (it should point to /redirect/1)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-022: BVA boundary+1 — n=2 takes different code path than n=1; catches off-by-one mutation on n==1 check
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_2_does_not_go_directly_to_get():
    r = client.get('/redirect/2', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
    location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert location != '/get', f'n=2 should not redirect directly to /get, got: {location}'
    assert '/redirect/1' in location, f'Expected /redirect/1 in location, got: {location}'

test_redirect_2_does_not_go_directly_to_get()

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_1_absolute_false_gives_relative_location():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert not location.startswith('http://'), f'Expected relative URL, got: {location}'
    assert not location.startswith('https://'), f'Expected relative URL, got: {location}'
    assert location == '/get'

test_redirect_1_absolute_false_gives_relative_location()

def test_redirect_1_absolute_true_gives_absolute_location():
